Live-run status-overlay CSS (issue #219), injected before </style> only on the non-null path.\n286\t    // The spinner is a pure CSS @keyframes rotation (no external image), inherently distinct from a\n287\t    // settled status's static glyph. `.status-<word>` colours mirror the log viewer's status palette.\n288\t    private const string StatusOverlayStyle = \"\"\"\n289\t\n290\t  #status-overlays { position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 9; }\n291\t  .status-badge { position: absolute; box-sizing: border-box; width: 18px; height: 18px;\n292\t                  border-radius: 50%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;\n293\t                  font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; color: #0b0f14;\n294\t                  border: 1px solid #0b0f14; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }\n295\t  .status-passed { background: #3fb950; }\n296\t  .status-failed { background: #f85149; color: #ffffff; }\n297\t  .status-needs-human { background: #d29922; }\n298\t  .status-pending, .status-blocked, .status-unknown { background: #30363d; color: #8aa0b3; }\n299\t  .status-spinner { background: transparent; border: 2px solid #243343; border-top-color: #7fdbff;\n300\t                    animation: status-spin 0.8s linear infinite; }\n301\t  @keyframes status-spin { to { transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(360deg); } }\n302\t\"\"\";\n303\t\n304\t    // Live-run status-overlay JavaScript (issue #219), injected before `let pz = null;` only on the\n305\t    // non-null path. Corner-anchored HTML badges OUTSIDE the SVG (mirroring the #bar/#legend overlays),\n306\t    // one per node id in the embedded #node-statuses side-table, re-anchored on every pan/zoom/resize.\n307\t    private const string StatusOverlayScript = \"\"\"\n308\t// --- live per-node status overlay (issue #219) -------------------------------------------------\n309\t// Corner-anchored status badges rendered as HTML overlay divs OUTSIDE the SVG (mirrors the #bar /\n310\t// #legend overlays), one per node id in the embedded #node-statuses side-table. A \"running\" node\n311\t// gets an animated CSS spinner; every settled status gets a static glyph. Because the badges live in\n312\t// screen space (not inside the SVG), they are re-anchored to each node's on-screen box\n313\t// (getBoundingClientRect) on every svg-pan-zoom pan / zoom + resize — wired below. Mirrors\n314\t// addTaskContainerOverlays' technique: it runs on the SAME SVG mermaid.render just produced.\n315\tconst nodeStatuses = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('node-statuses').textContent);\n316\tlet statusBadges = [];\n317\t\n318\tfunction statusGlyph(status) {\n319\t  switch (status) {\n320\t    case 'passed': return '✓';       // U+2713 CHECK MARK\n321\t    case 'failed': return '✗';       // U+2717 BALLOT X\n322\t    case 'needs-human': return '?';\n323\t    default: return '·';             // pending / blocked / anything else — a STATIC settled dot, never the spinner\n324\t  }\n325\t}\n326\t\n327\t// Resolve a status-map id to its SVG element. Task containers and NON-empty plan-level brackets keep\n328\t// their raw id on the <g class=\"cluster\">; leaf check nodes (and an EMPTY plan bracket, which Mermaid\n329\t// draws as a plain node) are ided \"flowchart-<logicalId>-<counter>\", so fall back to that prefix.\n330\tfunction findStatusTarget(svgEl, id) {\n331\t  return svgEl.querySelector('[id=\"' + id + '\"]')\n332\t      || svgEl.querySelector('[id^=\"flowchart-' + id + '-\"]');\n333\t}\n334\t\n335\t// Build one badge per status entry into a fixed overlay layer (created once). Each badge stays hidden\n336\t// until positionStatusBadges places it, so a badge whose node is off-screen never flashes at (0,0).\n337\tfunction addStatusOverlays(svgEl) {\n338\t  let layer = document.getElementById('status-overlays');\n339\t  if (!layer) { layer = document.createElement('div'); layer.id = 'status-overlays'; document.body.appendChild(layer); }\n340\t  layer.innerHTML = '';\n341\t  statusBadges = [];\n342\t  for (const [id, status] of Object.entries(nodeStatuses)) {\n343\t    const target = findStatusTarget(svgEl, id);\n344\t    if (!target) continue; // id not present in this render — no badge (defensive)\n345\t    const badge = document.createElement('div');\n346\t    if (status === 'running') {\n347\t      badge.className = 'status-badge status-spinner';\n348\t    } else {\n349\t      badge.className = 'status-badge status-' + status;\n350\t      badge.textContent = statusGlyph(status);\n351\t    }\n352\t    badge.setAttribute('aria-label', id + ': ' + status);\n353\t    badge.style.display = 'none';\n354\t    layer.appendChild(badge);\n355\t    statusBadges.push({ el: badge, target: target });\n356\t  }\n357\t  positionStatusBadges();\n358\t}\n359\t\n360\t// Re-anchor every badge to the top-right corner of its node's CURRENT on-screen box. Called after the\n361\t// overlay is built and again on every pan / zoom / resize so the badges track the diagram exactly.\n362\tfunction positionStatusBadges() {\n363\t  for (const b of statusBadges) {\n364\t    const r = b.target.getBoundingClientRect();\n365\t    if (r.width === 0 && r.height === 0) { b.el.style.display = 'none'; continue; }\n366\t    b.el.style.display = '';\n367\t    b.el.style.left = r.right + 'px';\n368\t    b.el.style.top = r.top + 'px';\n369\t  }\n370\t}\n371\t\"\"\";\n372\t\n373\t    // __SOURCE_SHA256__ is filled with a lowercase-hex hash (no escaping needed). __GRAPH_SOURCE__\n374\t    // is filled with the verbatim Mermaid text inside a raw-text <script> element (see remarks).\n375\t    // __TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__ is filled with a JSON object (container id -> folder path).\n376\t    // __SEARCH_INDEX__ is filled with a JSON object (node id -> visible label) by\n377\t    // BuildSearchIndexJson — currently always \"{}\" (stub; see class remarks, \"Search box\").\n378\t    private const string Template = \"\"\"\n379\t<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256=__SOURCE_SHA256__ -->\n380\t<!doctype html>\n381\t<html lang=\"en\">\n382\t<head>\n383\t<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n384\t<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n385\t<title>Guardrails — task/guardrail DAG</title>\n386\t<style>\n387\t  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; background: #0b0f14; color: #d6deeb;\n388\t               font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; overflow: hidden; }\n389\t  #bar { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; z-index: 10; display: flex; gap: 6px; }\n390\t  #bar button { background: #121a24; color: #d6deeb; border: 1px solid #243343;\n391\t                border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 10px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; }\n392\t  #bar button:hover { border-color: #7fdbff; }\n393\t  #stage { width: 100vw; height: 100vh; }\n394\t  #stage svg { width: 100vw; height: 100vh; max-width: none !important; }\n395\t  #hint { position: fixed; bottom: 8px; left: 8px; color: #5b6b7b; font-size: 12px;\n396\t          max-width: 90vw; }\n397\t  #legend { position: fixed; top: 8px; right: 8px; z-index: 10; background: #121a24;\n398\t            border: 1px solid #243343; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px;\n399\t            font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; }\n400\t  #legend .swatch { display: inline-block; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px;\n401\t                    margin-right: 6px; }\n402\t  #search-box { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); z-index: 10;\n403\t                display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: #121a24;\n404\t                border: 1px solid #243343; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 10px; }\n405\t  #search-box input { background: #0b0f14; color: #d6deeb; border: 1px solid #243343;\n406\t                       border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 13px; width: 220px; }\n407\t  #search-box button { background: #121a24; color: #d6deeb; border: 1px solid #243343;\n408\t                        border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; }\n409\t  #search-box button:hover { border-color: #7fdbff; }\n410\t  #search-count { color: #5b6b7b; font-size: 12px; min-width: 48px; text-align: center; }\n411\t  .search-match > rect, .search-match > polygon { stroke: #7fdbff !important; stroke-width: 3px !important; }\n412\t  .search-dim { opacity: 0.15; }\n413\t</style>\n414\t</head>\n415\t<body>\n416\t<div id=\"bar\">\n417\t  <button id=\"fit\">Fit</button>\n418\t  <button id=\"zin\">+</button>\n419\t  <button id=\"zout\">&minus;</button>\n420\t  <button id=\"fs\">Fullscreen</button>\n421\t</div>\n422\t<div id=\"stage\"></div>\n423\t<div id=\"search-box\">\n424\t  <input id=\"search-input\" type=\"text\" placeholder=\"Search nodes…\" autocomplete=\"off\" spellcheck=\"false\">\n425\t  <span id=\"search-count\"></span>\n426\t  <button id=\"search-prev\" title=\"Previous match\">&lsaquo;</button>\n427\t  <button id=\"search-next\" title=\"Next match\">&rsaquo;</button>\n428\t</div>\n429\t<div id=\"legend\">\n430\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#e6d7ff;border:1px solid #6f42c1;\"></span>\n431\t    <b>Preflight</b> &mdash; verified BEFORE the task's attempt loop; gates entry\n432\t    (dependency-delivery precondition)</div>\n433\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#fff3cd;border:1px solid #b8860b;\"></span>\n434\t    <b>Guardrail</b> &mdash; verified AFTER the task's action; must pass for the task to finish</div>\n435\t  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#d4edda;border:1px solid #2e7d32;\"></span>\n436\t    Plan-level containers (\"Full Flight Checks\" top, \"Terminal Gate\" bottom) run the same two\n437\t    checks once for the whole plan, at the very start and very end.</div>\n438\t</div>\n439\t<div id=\"hint\">scroll = zoom &middot; drag = pan &middot; Fit resets &middot; Fullscreen (or press F11).\n440\t  Node clicks open source files &mdash; serve via a local HTTP server (e.g.\n441\t  <code>python -m http.server</code>) for clicks to work; browsers block\n442\t  <code>file://&rarr;file://</code> navigation by default.\n443\t  On GitHub, diagram.md renders instead.</div>\n444\t\n445\t<script type=\"text/plain\" id=\"graph-source\">__GRAPH_SOURCE__</script>\n446\t<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"task-folder-targets\">__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__</script>\n447\t<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"search-index\">__SEARCH_INDEX__</script>\n448\t<script src=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js\"></script>\n449\t<script type=\"module\">\n450\timport mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';\n451\t\n452\tconst graph = document.getElementById('graph-source').textContent;\n453\tconst taskFolderTargets = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('task-folder-targets').textContent);\n454\tconst searchIndex = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('search-index').textContent);\n455\t// securityLevel 'loose' is required for the `click ... href` directives to open node sources;\n456\t// the content is the user's own local plan, served from file:// — not untrusted input.\n457\t// maxTextSize raises Mermaid's default 50 000-character source ceiling (issue #108): a large\n458\t// plan's DAG source easily exceeds it, and on overflow mermaid.render throws \"Maximum text size\n459\t// in diagram exceeded\" — landing every big plan in the catch-block \"could not render\" fallback.\n460\t// 5 000 000 covers DAGs far larger than any hand-reviewed plan while still bounding the parser.\n461\t// maxEdges raises Mermaid's default 500-edge ceiling for the same reason: a many-task plan fans\n462\t// out task→guardrail→done→dependent edges well past 500, and overflow throws \"Maximum number of\n463\t// edges exceeded\". Both ceilings must be lifted or a big plan still fails to render.\n464\tmermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'loose', maxTextSize: 5000000, maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: { useMaxWidth: false } });\n465\t\n466\t// Widen a wrapped cluster-title's foreignObject so a long kebab-case task name reflows onto\n467\t// FEWER lines instead of overflowing Mermaid's fixed header-strip reservation (issue\n468\t// cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Root cause, confirmed against the bundled mermaid@11.4.1 source\n469\t// (`src/rendering-util/createText.ts`'s `createText(el, text, { width = 200 })` default, which\n470\t// the plain flowchart \"rect\" cluster shape never overrides): a cluster's title <div> is always\n471\t// wrapped to a hardcoded 200px width regardless of the container's own — usually much wider —\n472\t// computed width, and dagre's LAYOUT PASS reserves header space for the container BEFORE that\n473\t// wrapped height is known, so it never grows to fit more than a couple of lines. A short label\n474\t// fits on one line inside 200px with room to spare (a healthy ~13px gap above the first leaf\n475\t// node, measured); a long name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) wraps to 2 or more\n476\t// lines, and each line beyond the first prints a full line-height PAST what dagre reserved —\n477\t// landing on top of the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned directly below.\n478\t//\n479\t// Two Mermaid config knobs were checked and ruled out first: `flowchart.htmlLabels` only toggles\n480\t// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer (not label width), and 11.4.1 has no documented\n481\t// `flowchart`/theme-variable option for cluster-label wrapping width — 200 is a hardcoded\n482\t// parameter default the cluster-shape renderer never overrides, not a configurable value.\n483\t//\n484\t// The fix instead re-wraps the SAME text into fewer lines post-render: a task container is\n485\t// normally already wider than 200px (dagre sized it to fit its leaf content), so letting the\n486\t// identical label reflow at (up to) the container's own width almost always drops it to one\n487\t// line, which needs LESS height than Mermaid's original wrap — never more. That means this can\n488\t// only ever shrink the label's footprint, never grow it, so no other node/edge/container ever\n489\t// needs to move to make room. Verified headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names,\n490\t// container widths from ~230px to ~1100px, wraps from 2 to 3 lines): every case converged to one\n491\t// line with the same healthy negative gap a short, never-wrapped label already has; every\n492\t// already-fits-on-one-line label (including every task in the golden `hello-guardrails` example)\n493\t// was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n494\tfunction fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl) {\n495\t  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n496\t  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n497\t    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n498\t    if (!label) continue;\n499\t    const fo = label.querySelector('foreignObject');\n500\t    const div = fo ? fo.querySelector('div') : null;\n501\t    if (!fo || !div) continue;\n502\t\n503\t    const currentWidth = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('width')) || 0;\n504\t    const currentHeight = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('height')) || 0;\n505\t    if (currentWidth <= 0 || currentHeight <= 0) continue;\n506\t\n507\t    // scrollWidth/scrollHeight are LOCAL layout-box measurements in the foreignObject's own\n508\t    // SVG-user-unit coordinate system — deliberately NOT the screen-space rect API (see class\n509\t    // remarks): a screen-space read is affected by every ancestor SVG transform (dagre's per-node\n510\t    // translate, the pan-zoom viewport's zoom/pan matrix), so it would be misleading compared\n511\t    // against the foreignObject's own width/height attributes. Measure the label's natural\n512\t    // single-line width by temporarily lifting the wrap constraint Mermaid applied, then restore\n513\t    // it immediately.\n514\t    const savedInline = div.getAttribute('style');\n515\t    div.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n516\t    div.style.width = 'auto';\n517\t    div.style.maxWidth = 'none';\n518\t    // +2px safety buffer: scrollWidth can round down a hair short of the true subpixel width\n519\t    // needed for one line (observed empirically — re-applying the exact measured value as a\n520\t    // fixed width sometimes still wrapped to 2 lines by a fraction of a pixel).\n521\t    const naturalWidth = div.scrollWidth + 2;\n522\t    div.setAttribute('style', savedInline); // restore Mermaid's original wrapped styling\n523\t\n524\t    if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue; // already fits on one line — untouched\n525\t\n526\t    // Never widen past the cluster's own body (leave a small margin) — the container's leaf\n527\t    // content already determined this width, so the label can use up to it without ever moving\n528\t    // a leaf node, edge, or sibling container. Never NARROWER than Mermaid's original width either\n529\t    // — this only ever grows the box.\n530\t    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n531\t    const newWidth = Math.min(naturalWidth, Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16));\n532\t\n533\t    div.style.whiteSpace = 'break-spaces';\n534\t    div.style.display = 'table';\n535\t    div.style.width = newWidth + 'px';\n536\t    div.style.maxWidth = newWidth + 'px';\n537\t    const newHeight = div.scrollHeight;\n538\t\n539\t    if (newHeight >= currentHeight) {\n540\t      // Widening did not actually reduce the wrapped height (the cluster is too narrow to fit\n541\t      // even one more character per line) — revert rather than risk an oddly-proportioned label.\n542\t      div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\n543\t      continue;\n544\t    }\n545\t\n546\t    fo.setAttribute('width', String(newWidth));\n547\t    fo.setAttribute('height', String(newHeight));\n548\t\n549\t    // Mermaid centers the label group on the cluster's horizontal midpoint via\n550\t    // `translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y)`; widening the box without re-centering would shift it\n551\t    // left of center, so shift the existing translate by half the width delta to keep it on the\n552\t    // SAME midpoint. The label's y stays fixed — only its height shrank, so its bottom edge\n553\t    // simply moves UP, further from the first leaf node, never displacing it.\n554\t    const transform = label.getAttribute('transform') || '';\n555\t    const match = transform.match(/translate\\(([-\\d.eE]+)\\s*,\\s*([-\\d.eE]+)\\)/);\n556\t    if (match) {\n557\t      const oldX = parseFloat(match[1]);\n558\t      const deltaCenter = (newWidth - currentWidth) / 2;\n559\t      label.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${oldX - deltaCenter}, ${match[2]})`);\n560\t    }\n561\t  }\n562\t}\n563\t\n564\t// Inject a real clickable overlay on each task container's TITLE/LABEL ROW (issue #232/#233\n565\t// superseded, issue #235). Mermaid never fires a `click` directive on a subgraph/cluster element,\n566\t// and an anchor NODE inside the container gets packed into whatever sliver of space dagre's own\n567\t// layout leaves — useless for a content-dense container. The title band is different: Mermaid\n568\t// ALWAYS renders a cluster as exactly two children, a background <rect> then a <g\n569\t// class=\"cluster-label\">, with the label in its own reserved header strip above any leaf content —\n570\t// so a full-width band from the cluster's top down to just past the label's bottom edge is empty BY\n571\t// CONSTRUCTION, regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has. Must run AFTER\n572\t// fixWrappedClusterLabels (above): the band height is measured from the label's CURRENT bbox, so\n573\t// a label that fixWrappedClusterLabels already shrank back to one line gets a correspondingly\n574\t// short band, not one sized for its original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n575\tfunction addTaskContainerOverlays(svgEl) {\n576\t  const ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';\n577\t  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n578\t  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n579\t    const target = taskFolderTargets[cluster.id];\n580\t    if (!target) continue; // not a task container (e.g. plan_preflights/plan_guardrails), or no map entry\n581\t    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n582\t    if (!label) continue;\n583\t\n584\t    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n585\t    const labelBox = label.getBBox();\n586\t    const bandHeight = (labelBox.y + labelBox.height) - clusterBox.y + 8; // small padding below the title\n587\t\n588\t    const a = document.createElementNS(ns, 'a');\n589\t    a.setAttribute('href', target);\n590\t    a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');\n591\t    a.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open task folder: ' + target);\n592\t\n593\t    const rect = document.createElementNS(ns, 'rect');\n594\t    rect.setAttribute('x', String(clusterBox.x));\n595\t    rect.setAttribute('y', String(clusterBox.y));\n596\t    rect.setAttribute('width', String(clusterBox.width));\n597\t    rect.setAttribute('height', String(bandHeight));\n598\t    // Inline style (not the `fill` ATTRIBUTE) deliberately: Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n599\t    // carries a rule like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}` that colors every cluster's\n600\t    // background rect. Since this overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group (so it stays in\n601\t    // the same paint context as the background rect it sits atop), that same selector matches it\n602\t    // too — and a CSS class/tag selector beats a plain presentation attribute, so `fill=\"transparent\"`\n603\t    // as an attribute got silently overridden, painting a solid theme-colored bar over the title text.\n604\t    // An inline style wins over any external/embedded stylesheet rule (short of `!important`), so it\n605\t    // reliably stays invisible regardless of Mermaid's theme.\n606\t    rect.style.fill = 'transparent';\n607\t    rect.style.cursor = 'pointer';\n608\t\n609\t    a.appendChild(rect);\n610\t    // Append as the LAST child — do NOT prepend as the first child. A cluster's only two original\n611\t    // children are its background <rect> then its .cluster-label group (in that paint order).\n612\t    // Appending puts the overlay on top of the background rect (so it is actually clickable)\n613\t    // without covering the label text visually (the rect is transparent either way) — prepending\n614\t    // instead would put the overlay BEHIND the background rect (which becomes second-in-order and\n615\t    // paints over it), silently blocking every click.\n616\t    cluster.appendChild(a);\n617\t  }\n618\t}\n619\t\n620\t// Diagram search (issue #220): substring-matches the typed query (case-insensitive) against every\n621\t// entry in `searchIndex` (id -> visible label, built by BuildSearchIndexJson — see class remarks),\n622\t// toggles each matching node's class to 'search-match' and every other node's to 'search-dim' (pure\n623\t// class toggling, no Mermaid re-render), updates the \"N of M\" counter, and auto pans/zooms the FIRST\n624\t// match into view via the SAME pan-zoom instance API positionStatusBadges' overlay already uses:\n625\t// pz.getPan(), pz.getSizes(), pz.pan({ x, y }), pz.zoom(z).\n626\t// STUB (deliberate TDD red — see BuildSearchIndexJson): searchIndex is always empty until\n627\t// 08-implement-diagram-search-box lands the real parsing, so this never has real work to do yet.\n628\tfunction runSearch(query) {\n629\t  throw new Error('NotImplementedException: diagram search (issue #220) is not implemented yet');\n630\t}\n631\t\n632\tlet pz = null;\n633\ttry {\n634\t  const { svg } = await mermaid.render('dag', graph);\n635\t  document.getElementById('stage').innerHTML = svg;\n636\t  const el = document.querySelector('#stage svg');\n637\t  el.setAttribute('width', '100vw');\n638\t  el.setAttribute('height', '100vh');\n639\t  fixWrappedClusterLabels(el);\n640\t  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\n641\t  pz = svgPanZoom(el, { zoomEnabled: true, controlIconsEnabled: false, fit: true, center: true,\n642\t                        minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\n643\t  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\n644\t} catch (e) {\n645\t  // Surface the actual failure (offline CDN, or a Mermaid limit we have not yet lifted) instead of\n646\t  // guessing — a generic \"offline?\" message sent every big-plan #108 failure down the wrong path.\n647\t  const detail = (e && e.message) ? String(e.message) : String(e);\n648\t  const p = document.createElement('p');\n649\t  p.style.padding = '1rem';\n650\t  p.textContent = 'Could not render the diagram: ' + detail +\n651\t    ' — the DAG source is embedded in this page, and diagram.md renders on GitHub.';\n652\t  const stage = document.getElementById('stage');\n653\t  stage.innerHTML = '';\n654\t  stage.appendChild(p);\n655\t}\n656\t\n657\tdocument.getElementById('fit').onclick  = () => { if (pz) { pz.fit(); pz.center(); } };\n658\tdocument.getElementById('zin').onclick  = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(1.3); };\n659\tdocument.getElementById('zout').onclick = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(0.77); };\n660\tdocument.getElementById('fs').onclick   = () => document.documentElement.requestFullscreen();\n661\t\n662\tdocument.getElementById('search-input').addEventListener('input', (e) => runSearch(e.target.value));\n663\tdocument.getElementById('search-prev').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\n664\tdocument.getElementById('search-next').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\n665\t</script>\n666\t</body>\n667\t</html>\n668\t\"\"\";\n669\t}\n670\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0b7c1cb6-24d8-455e-aa6d-0c4314ad8825","uuid":"e91bdabf-be67-44f0-af0c-9659e689186b","timestamp":"2026-07-07T17:23:58.690Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\David\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\guardrails-worktrees\\diagram-live-status-and-search-80c8913d\\33574b73\\03-author-tests-diagram-observer\\attempt-1\\src\\Guardrails.Core\\Graph\\HtmlDiagramRenderer.cs","content":"using System.Text.Encodings.Web;\nusing System.Text.Json;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Renders the local-viewing companion to <c>diagram.md</c>: a self-contained\n/// <c>diagram.html</c> that displays the SAME Mermaid DAG with pan / zoom / fullscreen, so a\n/// large task+guardrail graph is actually navigable on disk (GitHub renders <c>diagram.md</c>\n/// but offers no navigation). Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its <c>source-sha256</c>\n/// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33).\n/// </summary>\n/// <remarks>\n/// <para>\n/// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"text/plain\"&gt;</c> element and read back via <c>textContent</c> — never\n/// interpolated into a JS string. This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a\n/// backtick, <c>${</c>, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <c>&lt;script&gt;</c> element's\n/// content is \"raw text\" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte.\n/// This is safe because <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> HTML-escapes every label (so <c>&lt;</c>\n/// becomes <c>&amp;lt;</c>), meaning the source can never contain <c>&lt;/script&gt;</c>.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The <c>source-sha256</c> provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before\n/// <c>&lt;!doctype html&gt;</c>) so the same <c>\\A</c>-anchored reader that validates\n/// <c>diagram.md</c> validates this file too (<c>graph --check</c>). A comment before the\n/// doctype does not trigger quirks mode.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs\n/// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the\n/// LOCAL artifact; <c>diagram.md</c> remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets)\n/// is a possible follow-up.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Legend overlay.</b> A corner-anchored <c>#legend</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>\n/// (<c>position: fixed</c>), mirroring the existing <c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> overlay divs, renders\n/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.LegendMarkdown\"/>'s content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native\n/// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN —\n/// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\" overlapping the real DAG — so\n/// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from\n/// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on <c>source-sha256</c>.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233\n/// superseded, issue #235).</b> A Mermaid <c>click</c> directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster\n/// element (upstream limitation; see <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> remarks), and the first fix\n/// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre\n/// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container\n/// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail\n/// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves: for every\n/// <c>g.cluster</c> element whose id starts with <c>task_</c>, compute a full-width band from the\n/// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its <c>.cluster-label</c>'s bottom edge (Mermaid\n/// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION\n/// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and\n/// append a real <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c>\n/// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its\n/// background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c> then its <c>.cluster-label</c> group, so appending puts the\n/// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text\n/// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely\n/// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's <c>g.cluster</c> — the overlay can never\n/// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data\n/// this script needs (<see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) is embedded as a small JSON\n/// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"&gt;</c> element read back via <c>textContent</c> (same\n/// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping\n/// hazards).\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject\n/// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow).</b> Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title\n/// <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>'s plain\n/// flowchart cluster shape never overrides <c>createText</c>'s <c>width = 200</c> default,\n/// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout\n/// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a\n/// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines\n/// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned\n/// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — <c>flowchart.htmlLabels</c> only toggles\n/// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label\n/// wrap width. The fix (the <c>fixWrappedClusterLabels</c> function, run AFTER\n/// <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's\n/// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the\n/// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already\n/// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than\n/// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. Verified\n/// headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names): every wrapped case converged to one line\n/// with the same healthy gap a never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label\n/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Search box (issue #220).</b> A fixed-position <c>#search-box</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> (same\n/// overlay technique as <c>#legend</c>/<c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> and the status badges) is emitted\n/// UNCONDITIONALLY — unlike the live status overlay above, search does not depend on the\n/// <c>nodeStatuses</c> parameter (see <see cref=\"Render\"/>) being non-null, so it is present on both\n/// the static <c>graph</c> output and the live/final run diagrams. The search-matching data (every\n/// node id + visible label) is embedded the same way as\n/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/> — a <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"\n/// id=\"search-index\"&gt;</c> side-table read back via <c>textContent</c> — built by\n/// <see cref=\"BuildSearchIndexJson\"/>. <b>This is a stub</b>: it always emits an empty object, and\n/// the embedded <c>runSearch</c> script throws (a deliberate TDD red for\n/// <c>08-implement-diagram-search-box</c>) — see that method's remarks.\n/// </para>\n/// </remarks>\npublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer\n{\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Build the <c>diagram.html</c> document for <paramref name=\"mermaidSource\"/> (the exact\n    /// text rendered into <c>diagram.md</c>, including the <c>flowchart TD</c> header and the\n    /// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> lines) stamped with <paramref name=\"sourceHash\"/>. <paramref\n    /// name=\"taskFolderTargets\"/> is the task-container-id → plan-relative-folder-path map (see\n    /// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) the embedded title-band overlay script uses\n    /// to resolve each container's click target (issue #235 — see class remarks).\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <param name=\"nodeStatuses\">\n    /// OPTIONAL live-run status map (issue #219): Mermaid node/container id → one of\n    /// <c>\"pending\"</c>, <c>\"running\"</c>, <c>\"passed\"</c>, <c>\"failed\"</c>, <c>\"needs-human\"</c>,\n    /// keyed by the SAME ids <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> emits (task containers <c>task_&lt;base&gt;</c>,\n    /// preflight/guardrail leaves <c>task_&lt;base&gt;_pf_&lt;n&gt;</c>/<c>task_&lt;base&gt;_gr_&lt;n&gt;</c>,\n    /// and the plan-level brackets <c>plan_preflights</c>/<c>plan_guardrails</c>). When non-null the\n    /// document additionally carries a per-node status-overlay badge (an animated spinner while\n    /// <c>running</c>, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once finished). When <c>null</c> (the static\n    /// <c>graph</c> command, which never runs live) the output is byte-identical to the pre-#219\n    /// three-argument render.\n    /// </param>\n    /// <param name=\"includeRefresh\">\n    /// INDEPENDENT of the status overlay (mirrors <c>LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)</c>):\n    /// when <paramref name=\"nodeStatuses\"/> is non-null AND this is <c>true</c> (the default,\n    /// the DURING-RUN diagram) a <c>&lt;meta http-equiv=\"refresh\" content=\"2\"&gt;</c> is emitted so a\n    /// plain <c>file://</c> view re-reads itself as the run progresses; when <c>false</c> (the FINAL\n    /// settled render wired at run-end by <c>06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand</c>) the overlay\n    /// is still emitted but the refresh tag is not. Ignored when <paramref name=\"nodeStatuses\"/> is null.\n    /// </param>\n    public static string Render(\n        string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets,\n        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? nodeStatuses = null, bool includeRefresh = true)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(mermaidSource);\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty(sourceHash);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(taskFolderTargets);\n\n        // Newline-normalize so the file is byte-identical across OSes (mirrors the renderer/hash).\n        string source = mermaidSource\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .TrimEnd('\\n');\n\n        // Encoder that escapes NOTHING beyond what JSON strictly requires (default System.Text.Json\n        // escapes '<', '>', '&', etc. as \\uXXXX for HTML safety, which is unnecessary here — the\n        // JSON sits inside a <script type=\"application/json\"> element, read back via textContent,\n        // exactly like the Mermaid source above — but using the unsafe-relaxed encoder keeps a\n        // task-id containing e.g. \"&\" readable in the raw HTML source without changing behavior).\n        string targetsJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(taskFolderTargets, new JsonSerializerOptions\n        {\n            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n        });\n\n        // Search box (issue #220) is UNCONDITIONAL — unlike the status overlay below, it does not\n        // depend on nodeStatuses, so it is part of the base template replacement every call performs.\n        string searchIndexJson = BuildSearchIndexJson(source);\n\n        string html = Template\n            .Replace(\"__SOURCE_SHA256__\", sourceHash, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"__GRAPH_SOURCE__\", source, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__\", targetsJson, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"__SEARCH_INDEX__\", searchIndexJson, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Live-run status overlay (issue #219) is OPTIONAL: when nodeStatuses is null (the static\n        // `graph` command, which never runs live) the template is emitted UNCHANGED, so the output\n        // stays byte-identical to the pre-#219 three-argument render. When provided, inject the\n        // per-node status badges + CSS, the node-statuses side-table, and — when includeRefresh — the\n        // auto-reload meta tag (see InjectStatusOverlay).\n        if (nodeStatuses is not null)\n        {\n            html = InjectStatusOverlay(html, nodeStatuses, includeRefresh);\n        }\n\n        // Normalize the full output — the template raw-string literal (and the injected blocks above)\n        // pick up \\r\\n when the file is checked out with CRLF on Windows; the mermaid source is\n        // already normalized above.\n        return html\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Build the diagram-search (issue #220) id-to-label side-table embedded as\n    /// <c>__SEARCH_INDEX__</c>, mirroring the <c>__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__</c> JSON side-table (see\n    /// class remarks, \"Search box\"). <c>08-implement-diagram-search-box</c> will parse <paramref\n    /// name=\"mermaidSource\"/> for every node/container id and its visible label — the SAME\n    /// <c>id[label]</c> shapes <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/>'s <c>AppendTaskContainer</c>/\n    /// <c>AppendCheckNodes</c> emit (task containers, preflight/guardrail leaves, and the two\n    /// plan-level brackets) — into real id-&gt;label entries.\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// <b>STUB (deliberate TDD red).</b> This task (<c>07-author-tests-diagram-search-box</c>)\n    /// authors the failing tests and the minimal search-box wiring only — it always returns an empty\n    /// object regardless of <paramref name=\"mermaidSource\"/>, so the search box never actually finds\n    /// a match until the real parsing lands. Returning <c>\"{}\"</c> rather than throwing keeps every\n    /// existing <see cref=\"Render\"/> call (including every pre-existing golden/round-trip fixture)\n    /// working unchanged — only the search-specific tests that assert the index is POPULATED are\n    /// meant to fail against this stub.\n    /// </remarks>\n    private static string BuildSearchIndexJson(string mermaidSource) => \"{}\";\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Inject the live-run status overlay (issue #219) into the base <paramref name=\"html\"/>: the\n    /// per-node status-badge markup + CSS, the <c>#node-statuses</c> JSON side-table, and — when\n    /// <paramref name=\"includeRefresh\"/> — the <c>&lt;meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"&gt;</c> auto-reload\n    /// tag. Called ONLY on the non-null path (see <see cref=\"Render\"/>), so the static-graph output is\n    /// left byte-identical.\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// Mirrors the existing title-band overlay's post-render-script technique: the badges are HTML\n    /// overlay <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>s (like <c>#bar</c>/<c>#legend</c>) rendered OUTSIDE the SVG and\n    /// anchored to each node's on-screen box via <c>getBoundingClientRect()</c>. Because they live in\n    /// screen space rather than inside the SVG, they are re-anchored on every <c>svg-pan-zoom</c>\n    /// pan/zoom (wired through the pan-zoom instance's <c>onPan</c>/<c>onZoom</c> callbacks) and on\n    /// window resize. A <c>running</c> node shows an animated CSS-<c>@keyframes</c> spinner (no\n    /// external image); every other (settled) status shows a static glyph. The auto-reload tag is\n    /// INDEPENDENT of the overlay (mirrors <c>LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)</c>'s\n    /// during-run vs final duality) — present for the during-run diagram, dropped for the final\n    /// settled render.\n    /// </remarks>\n    private static string InjectStatusOverlay(\n        string html, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeStatuses, bool includeRefresh)\n    {\n        // Same relaxed-encoder side-table treatment as taskFolderTargets: a JSON object (node id ->\n        // status word) read back via textContent from a <script type=\"application/json\"> element.\n        string statusesJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(nodeStatuses, new JsonSerializerOptions\n        {\n            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n        });\n\n        // Auto-reload tag (during-run only) right after the viewport meta in <head>.\n        if (includeRefresh)\n        {\n            html = html.Replace(\n                \"<meta name=\\\"viewport\\\" content=\\\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\\\">\",\n                \"<meta name=\\\"viewport\\\" content=\\\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\\\">\\n\"\n                    + \"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\" content=\\\"2\\\">\",\n                StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        }\n\n        // Status-badge CSS (spinner @keyframes + per-status colours) just before </style>.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"</style>\", StatusOverlayStyle + \"\\n</style>\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // The node id -> status side-table, mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table, placed just\n        // before the svg-pan-zoom script so it is already in the DOM when the module script reads it.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"<script src=\\\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom\",\n            \"<script type=\\\"application/json\\\" id=\\\"node-statuses\\\">\" + statusesJson + \"</script>\\n\"\n                + \"<script src=\\\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // The overlay functions, defined just before `let pz = null;` (module scope, after the graph/\n        // targets consts, so they can read #node-statuses and be called from the try block below).\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"let pz = null;\", StatusOverlayScript + \"\\n\\nlet pz = null;\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Build the overlay on the SAME SVG mermaid.render just produced, right after the title-band\n        // overlay (so it measures the SVG in its final, wrap-corrected shape).\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\",\n            \"  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\\n  addStatusOverlays(el);\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Re-anchor the (screen-space) badges whenever the pan-zoom viewport pans or zooms.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\",\n            \"minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3,\\n\"\n                + \"                        onPan: positionStatusBadges, onZoom: positionStatusBadges });\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // ...and on resize, plus one initial placement now that pan-zoom has fit the diagram.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\",\n            \"  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); positionStatusBadges(); });\\n\"\n                + \"  positionStatusBadges();\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        return html;\n    }\n\n    // Live-run status-overlay CSS (issue #219), injected before </style> only on the non-null path.\n    // The spinner is a pure CSS @keyframes rotation (no external image), inherently distinct from a\n    // settled status's static glyph. `.status-<word>` colours mirror the log viewer's status palette.\n    private const string StatusOverlayStyle = \"\"\"\n\n  #status-overlays { position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 9; }\n  .status-badge { position: absolute; box-sizing: border-box; width: 18px; height: 18px;\n                  border-radius: 50%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;\n                  font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; color: #0b0f14;\n                  border: 1px solid #0b0f14; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }\n  .status-passed { background: #3fb950; }\n  .status-failed { background: #f85149; color: #ffffff; }\n  .status-needs-human { background: #d29922; }\n  .status-pending, .status-blocked, .status-unknown { background: #30363d; color: #8aa0b3; }\n  .status-spinner { background: transparent; border: 2px solid #243343; border-top-color: #7fdbff;\n                    animation: status-spin 0.8s linear infinite; }\n  @keyframes status-spin { to { transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(360deg); } }\n\"\"\";\n\n    // Live-run status-overlay JavaScript (issue #219), injected before `let pz = null;` only on the\n    // non-null path. Corner-anchored HTML badges OUTSIDE the SVG (mirroring the #bar/#legend overlays),\n    // one per node id in the embedded #node-statuses side-table, re-anchored on every pan/zoom/resize.\n    private const string StatusOverlayScript = \"\"\"\n// --- live per-node status overlay (issue #219) -------------------------------------------------\n// Corner-anchored status badges rendered as HTML overlay divs OUTSIDE the SVG (mirrors the #bar /\n// #legend overlays), one per node id in the embedded #node-statuses side-table. A \"running\" node\n// gets an animated CSS spinner; every settled status gets a static glyph. Because the badges live in\n// screen space (not inside the SVG), they are re-anchored to each node's on-screen box\n// (getBoundingClientRect) on every svg-pan-zoom pan / zoom + resize — wired below. Mirrors\n// addTaskContainerOverlays' technique: it runs on the SAME SVG mermaid.render just produced.\nconst nodeStatuses = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('node-statuses').textContent);\nlet statusBadges = [];\n\nfunction statusGlyph(status) {\n  switch (status) {\n    case 'passed': return '✓';       // U+2713 CHECK MARK\n    case 'failed': return '✗';       // U+2717 BALLOT X\n    case 'needs-human': return '?';\n    default: return '·';             // pending / blocked / anything else — a STATIC settled dot, never the spinner\n  }\n}\n\n// Resolve a status-map id to its SVG element. Task containers and NON-empty plan-level brackets keep\n// their raw id on the <g class=\"cluster\">; leaf check nodes (and an EMPTY plan bracket, which Mermaid\n// draws as a plain node) are ided \"flowchart-<logicalId>-<counter>\", so fall back to that prefix.\nfunction findStatusTarget(svgEl, id) {\n  return svgEl.querySelector('[id=\"' + id + '\"]')\n      || svgEl.querySelector('[id^=\"flowchart-' + id + '-\"]');\n}\n\n// Build one badge per status entry into a fixed overlay layer (created once). Each badge stays hidden\n// until positionStatusBadges places it, so a badge whose node is off-screen never flashes at (0,0).\nfunction addStatusOverlays(svgEl) {\n  let layer = document.getElementById('status-overlays');\n  if (!layer) { layer = document.createElement('div'); layer.id = 'status-overlays'; document.body.appendChild(layer); }\n  layer.innerHTML = '';\n  statusBadges = [];\n  for (const [id, status] of Object.entries(nodeStatuses)) {\n    const target = findStatusTarget(svgEl, id);\n    if (!target) continue; // id not present in this render — no badge (defensive)\n    const badge = document.createElement('div');\n    if (status === 'running') {\n      badge.className = 'status-badge status-spinner';\n    } else {\n      badge.className = 'status-badge status-' + status;\n      badge.textContent = statusGlyph(status);\n    }\n    badge.setAttribute('aria-label', id + ': ' + status);\n    badge.style.display = 'none';\n    layer.appendChild(badge);\n    statusBadges.push({ el: badge, target: target });\n  }\n  positionStatusBadges();\n}\n\n// Re-anchor every badge to the top-right corner of its node's CURRENT on-screen box. Called after the\n// overlay is built and again on every pan / zoom / resize so the badges track the diagram exactly.\nfunction positionStatusBadges() {\n  for (const b of statusBadges) {\n    const r = b.target.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (r.width === 0 && r.height === 0) { b.el.style.display = 'none'; continue; }\n    b.el.style.display = '';\n    b.el.style.left = r.right + 'px';\n    b.el.style.top = r.top + 'px';\n  }\n}\n\"\"\";\n\n    // __SOURCE_SHA256__ is filled with a lowercase-hex hash (no escaping needed). __GRAPH_SOURCE__\n    // is filled with the verbatim Mermaid text inside a raw-text <script> element (see remarks).\n    // __TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__ is filled with a JSON object (container id -> folder path).\n    // __SEARCH_INDEX__ is filled with a JSON object (node id -> visible label) by\n    // BuildSearchIndexJson — currently always \"{}\" (stub; see class remarks, \"Search box\").\n    private const string Template = \"\"\"\n<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256=__SOURCE_SHA256__ -->\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n<title>Guardrails — task/guardrail DAG</title>\n<style>\n  html, body { margin: 0; color: #d6deeb; border: 1px solid #243343;\n                        border-radius: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 13px; }\n  #search-box button:hover { border-color: #7fdbff; }\n  #search-count { color: #5b6b7b; font-size: 12px; min-width: 48px; text-align: center; }\n  .search-match > rect, .search-match > polygon { stroke: #7fdbff !important; stroke-width: 3px !important; }\n  .search-dim { opacity: 0.15; }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<div id=\"bar\">\n  <button id=\"fit\">Fit</button>\n  <button id=\"zin\">+</button>\n  <button id=\"zout\">&minus;</button>\n  <button id=\"fs\">Fullscreen</button>\n</div>\n<div id=\"stage\"></div>\n<div id=\"search-box\">\n  <input id=\"search-input\" type=\"text\" placeholder=\"Search nodes…\" autocomplete=\"off\" spellcheck=\"false\">\n  <span id=\"search-count\"></span>\n  <button id=\"search-prev\" title=\"Previous match\">&lsaquo;</button>\n  <button id=\"search-next\" title=\"Next match\">&rsaquo;</button>\n</div>\n<div id=\"legend\">\n  <div><span class=\"swatch\" style=\"background:#e6d7ff;border:1px solid #6f42c1;\"></span>\n    <b>Preflight</b> &mdash; browsers block\n  <code>file://&rarr;file://</code> navigation by default.\n  On GitHub, diagram.md renders instead.</div>\n\n<script type=\"text/plain\" id=\"graph-source\">__GRAPH_SOURCE__</script>\n<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"task-folder-targets\">__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__</script>\n<script type=\"application/json\" id=\"search-index\">__SEARCH_INDEX__</script>\n<script src=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom@3.6.1/dist/svg-pan-zoom.min.js\"></script>\n<script type=\"module\">\nimport mermaid from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11.4.1/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs';\n\nconst graph = document.getElementById('graph-source').textContent;\nconst taskFolderTargets = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('task-folder-targets').textContent);\nconst searchIndex = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('search-index').textContent);\n// securityLevel 'loose' is required for the `click ... href` directives to open node sources;\n// the content is the user's own local plan, served from file:// — not untrusted input.\n// maxTextSize raises Mermaid's default 50 000-character source ceiling (issue #108): a large\n// plan's DAG source easily exceeds it, and on overflow mermaid.render throws \"Maximum text size\n// in diagram exceeded\" — landing every big plan in the catch-block \"could not render\" fallback.\n// 5 000 000 covers DAGs far larger than any hand-reviewed plan while still bounding the parser.\n// maxEdges raises Mermaid's default 500-edge ceiling for the same reason: a many-task plan fans\n// out task→guardrail→done→dependent edges well past 500, and overflow throws \"Maximum number of\n// edges exceeded\". Both ceilings must be lifted or a big plan still fails to render.\nmermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'loose', maxTextSize: 5000000, maxEdges: 100000, flowchart: { useMaxWidth: false } });\n\n// Widen a wrapped cluster-title's foreignObject so a long kebab-case task name reflows onto\n// FEWER lines instead of overflowing Mermaid's fixed header-strip reservation (issue\n// cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Root cause, confirmed against the bundled mermaid@11.4.1 source\n// (`src/rendering-util/createText.ts`'s `createText(el, text, { width = 200 })` default, which\n// the plain flowchart \"rect\" cluster shape never overrides): a cluster's title <div> is always\n// wrapped to a hardcoded 200px width regardless of the container's own — usually much wider —\n// computed width, and dagre's LAYOUT PASS reserves header space for the container BEFORE that\n// wrapped height is known, so it never grows to fit more than a couple of lines. A short label\n// fits on one line inside 200px with room to spare (a healthy ~13px gap above the first leaf\n// node, measured); a long name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) wraps to 2 or more\n// lines, and each line beyond the first prints a full line-height PAST what dagre reserved —\n// landing on top of the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned directly below.\n//\n// Two Mermaid config knobs were checked and ruled out first: `flowchart.htmlLabels` only toggles\n// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer (not label width), and 11.4.1 has no documented\n// `flowchart`/theme-variable option for cluster-label wrapping width — 200 is a hardcoded\n// parameter default the cluster-shape renderer never overrides, not a configurable value.\n//\n// The fix instead re-wraps the SAME text into fewer lines post-render: a task container is\n// normally already wider than 200px (dagre sized it to fit its leaf content), so letting the\n// identical label reflow at (up to) the container's own width almost always drops it to one\n// line, which needs LESS height than Mermaid's original wrap — never more. That means this can\n// only ever shrink the label's footprint, never grow it, so no other node/edge/container ever\n// needs to move to make room. Verified headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names,\n// container widths from ~230px to ~1100px, wraps from 2 to 3 lines): every case converged to one\n// line with the same healthy negative gap a short, never-wrapped label already has; every\n// already-fits-on-one-line label (including every task in the golden `hello-guardrails` example)\n// was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\nfunction fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl) {\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n    const fo = label.querySelector('foreignObject');\n    const div = fo ? fo.querySelector('div') : null;\n    if (!fo || !div) continue;\n\n    const currentWidth = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('width')) || 0;\n    const currentHeight = parseFloat(fo.getAttribute('height')) || 0;\n    if (currentWidth <= 0 || currentHeight <= 0) continue;\n\n    // scrollWidth/scrollHeight are LOCAL layout-box measurements in the foreignObject's own\n    // SVG-user-unit coordinate system — deliberately NOT the screen-space rect API (see class\n    // remarks): a screen-space read is affected by every ancestor SVG transform (dagre's per-node\n    // translate, the pan-zoom viewport's zoom/pan matrix), so it would be misleading compared\n    // against the foreignObject's own width/height attributes. Measure the label's natural\n    // single-line width by temporarily lifting the wrap constraint Mermaid applied, then restore\n    // it immediately.\n    const savedInline = div.getAttribute('style');\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    div.style.width = 'auto';\n    div.style.maxWidth = 'none';\n    // +2px safety buffer: scrollWidth can round down a hair short of the true subpixel width\n    // needed for one line (observed empirically — re-applying the exact measured value as a\n    // fixed width sometimes still wrapped to 2 lines by a fraction of a pixel).\n    const naturalWidth = div.scrollWidth + 2;\n    div.setAttribute('style', savedInline); // restore Mermaid's original wrapped styling\n\n    if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue; // already fits on one line — untouched\n\n    // Never widen past the cluster's own body (leave a small margin) — the container's leaf\n    // content already determined this width, so the label can use up to it without ever moving\n    // a leaf node, edge, or sibling container. Never NARROWER than Mermaid's original width either\n    // — this only ever grows the box.\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const newWidth = Math.min(naturalWidth, Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16));\n\n    div.style.whiteSpace = 'break-spaces';\n    div.style.display = 'table';\n    div.style.width = newWidth + 'px';\n    div.style.maxWidth = newWidth + 'px';\n    const newHeight = div.scrollHeight;\n\n    if (newHeight >= currentHeight) {\n      // Widening did not actually reduce the wrapped height (the cluster is too narrow to fit\n      // even one more character per line) — revert rather than risk an oddly-proportioned label.\n      div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    fo.setAttribute('width', String(newWidth));\n    fo.setAttribute('height', String(newHeight));\n\n    // Mermaid centers the label group on the cluster's horizontal midpoint via\n    // `translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y)`; widening the box without re-centering would shift it\n    // left of center, so shift the existing translate by half the width delta to keep it on the\n    // SAME midpoint. The label's y stays fixed — only its height shrank, so its bottom edge\n    // simply moves UP, further from the first leaf node, never displacing it.\n    const transform = label.getAttribute('transform') || '';\n    const match = transform.match(/translate\\(([-\\d.eE]+)\\s*,\\s*([-\\d.eE]+)\\)/);\n    if (match) {\n      const oldX = parseFloat(match[1]);\n      const deltaCenter = (newWidth - currentWidth) / 2;\n      label.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${oldX - deltaCenter}, ${match[2]})`);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Inject a real clickable overlay on each task container's TITLE/LABEL ROW (issue #232/#233\n// superseded, issue #235). Mermaid never fires a `click` directive on a subgraph/cluster element,\n// and an anchor NODE inside the container gets packed into whatever sliver of space dagre's own\n// layout leaves — useless for a content-dense container. The title band is different: Mermaid\n// ALWAYS renders a cluster as exactly two children, a background <rect> then a <g\n// class=\"cluster-label\">, with the label in its own reserved header strip above any leaf content —\n// so a full-width band from the cluster's top down to just past the label's bottom edge is empty BY\n// CONSTRUCTION, regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has. Must run AFTER\n// fixWrappedClusterLabels (above): the band height is measured from the label's CURRENT bbox, so\n// a label that fixWrappedClusterLabels already shrank back to one line gets a correspondingly\n// short band, not one sized for its original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\nfunction addTaskContainerOverlays(svgEl) {\n  const ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';\n  const clusters = svgEl.querySelectorAll('g.cluster');\n  for (const cluster of clusters) {\n    const target = taskFolderTargets[cluster.id];\n    if (!target) continue; // not a task container (e.g. plan_preflights/plan_guardrails), or no map entry\n    const label = cluster.querySelector('.cluster-label');\n    if (!label) continue;\n\n    const clusterBox = cluster.getBBox();\n    const labelBox = label.getBBox();\n    const bandHeight = (labelBox.y + labelBox.height) - clusterBox.y + 8; // small padding below the title\n\n    const a = document.createElementNS(ns, 'a');\n    a.setAttribute('href', target);\n    a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');\n    a.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open task folder: ' + target);\n\n    const rect = document.createElementNS(ns, 'rect');\n    rect.setAttribute('x', String(clusterBox.x));\n    rect.setAttribute('y', String(clusterBox.y));\n    rect.setAttribute('width', String(clusterBox.width));\n    rect.setAttribute('height', String(bandHeight));\n    // Inline style (not the `fill` ATTRIBUTE) deliberately: Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n    // carries a rule like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}` that colors every cluster's\n    // background rect. Since this overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group (so it stays in\n    // the same paint context as the background rect it sits atop), that same selector matches it\n    // too — and a CSS class/tag selector beats a plain presentation attribute, so `fill=\"transparent\"`\n    // as an attribute got silently overridden, painting a solid theme-colored bar over the title text.\n    // An inline style wins over any external/embedded stylesheet rule (short of `!important`), so it\n    // reliably stays invisible regardless of Mermaid's theme.\n    rect.style.fill = 'transparent';\n    rect.style.cursor = 'pointer';\n\n    a.appendChild(rect);\n    // Append as the LAST child — do NOT prepend as the first child. A cluster's only two original\n    // children are its background <rect> then its .cluster-label group (in that paint order).\n    // Appending puts the overlay on top of the background rect (so it is actually clickable)\n    // without covering the label text visually (the rect is transparent either way) — prepending\n    // instead would put the overlay BEHIND the background rect (which becomes second-in-order and\n    // paints over it), silently blocking every click.\n    cluster.appendChild(a);\n  }\n}\n\n// Diagram search (issue #220): substring-matches the typed query (case-insensitive) against every\n// entry in `searchIndex` (id -> visible label, built by BuildSearchIndexJson — see class remarks),\n// toggles each matching node's class to 'search-match' and every other node's to 'search-dim' (pure\n// class toggling, no Mermaid re-render), updates the \"N of M\" counter, and auto pans/zooms the FIRST\n// match into view via the SAME pan-zoom instance API positionStatusBadges' overlay already uses:\n// pz.getPan(), pz.getSizes(), pz.pan({ x, y }), pz.zoom(z).\n// STUB (deliberate TDD red — see BuildSearchIndexJson): searchIndex is always empty until\n// 08-implement-diagram-search-box lands the real parsing, so this never has real work to do yet.\nfunction runSearch(query) {\n  throw new Error('NotImplementedException: diagram search (issue #220) is not implemented yet');\n}\n\nlet pz = null;\ntry {\n  const { svg } = await mermaid.render('dag', graph);\n  document.getElementById('stage').innerHTML = svg;\n  const el = document.querySelector('#stage svg');\n  el.setAttribute('width', '100vw');\n  el.setAttribute('height', '100vh');\n  fixWrappedClusterLabels(el);\n  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\n  pz = svgPanZoom(el, { zoomEnabled: true, controlIconsEnabled: false, fit: true, center: true,\n                        minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\n  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\n} catch (e) {\n  // Surface the actual failure (offline CDN, or a Mermaid limit we have not yet lifted) instead of\n  // guessing — a generic \"offline?\" message sent every big-plan #108 failure down the wrong path.\n  const detail = (e && e.message) ? String(e.message) : String(e);\n  const p = document.createElement('p');\n  p.style.padding = '1rem';\n  p.textContent = 'Could not render the diagram: ' + detail +\n    ' — the DAG source is embedded in this page, and diagram.md renders on GitHub.';\n  const stage = document.getElementById('stage');\n  stage.innerHTML = '';\n  stage.appendChild(p);\n}\n\ndocument.getElementById('fit').onclick  = () => { if (pz) { pz.fit(); pz.center(); } };\ndocument.getElementById('zin').onclick  = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(1.3); };\ndocument.getElementById('zout').onclick = () => { if (pz) pz.zoomBy(0.77); };\ndocument.getElementById('fs').onclick   = () => document.documentElement.requestFullscreen();\n\ndocument.getElementById('search-input').addEventListener('input', (e) => runSearch(e.target.value));\ndocument.getElementById('search-prev').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\ndocument.getElementById('search-next').onclick = () => runSearch(document.getElementById('search-input').value);\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n\"\"\";\n}\n","numLines":670,"startLine":1,"totalLines":670}}}

A crash mid-write can leave a stray <c>*.tmp</c> but\n/// never a half-written target, so <c>state.json</c>/<c>run.json</c> are always either the\n/// old or the new content, never a torn blend.\n/// </summary>\npublic static class AtomicFile\n{\n    private static readonly UTF8Encoding Utf8NoBom = new(encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: false);\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Write <paramref name=\"content\"/> to <paramref name=\"path\"/> atomically: a sibling temp\n    /// file is written and flushed, then moved over the target (overwriting if present).\n    /// The parent directory is created if missing.\n    /// </summary>\n    public static void WriteAllText(string path, string content)\n    {\n        string directory = Path.GetDirectoryName(path)\n            ?? throw new ArgumentException($\"Path has no directory: {path}\", nameof(path));\n        Directory.CreateDirectory(directory);\n\n        // Keep the temp file in the same directory so the move is a same-volume rename.\n        string tempPath = Path.Combine(directory, $\".{Path.GetFileName(path)}.{Guid.NewGuid():N}.tmp\");\n\n        try\n        {\n            File.WriteAllText(tempPath, content, Utf8NoBom);\n            File.Move(tempPath, path, overwrite: true);\n        }\n        finally\n        {\n            // Best-effort cleanup if the move failed and left the temp behind.\n            if (File.Exists(tempPath))\n            {\n                try\n                {\n                    File.Delete(tempPath);\n                }\n                catch (IOException)\n                {\n                    // The stray temp is harmless; never fail the write over cleanup.\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n","numLines":51,"startLine":1,"totalLines":51}}}

It\n/// WRAPS the real observer, forwards every event verbatim, and after certain events re-renders the\n/// diagram from an in-memory per-node status map via <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/>'s\n/// optional <c>nodeStatuses</c> parameter (02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer):\n/// <list type=\"bullet\">\n///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskStarting\"/> the task's CONTAINER node flips to <c>\"running\"</c>\n///     (coarse — per-check granularity for a task's own checks is unnecessary here since they have\n///     not run yet; it is driven by <see cref=\"GuardrailFinished\"/> instead).</item>\n///   <item>On <see cref=\"GuardrailFinished\"/> only the SPECIFIC preflight/guardrail leaf node that\n///     just finished flips to <c>\"passed\"</c>/<c>\"failed\"</c> — never the whole task container.</item>\n///   <item>On <see cref=\"TaskFinished\"/> the task's container flips to its settled status\n///     (<c>\"passed\"</c>/<c>\"failed\"</c>/<c>\"needs-human\"</c>, mapped from <see cref=\"TaskOutcome\"/>).</item>\n/// </list>\n///\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Design choice (this task's either/or):</b> the Mermaid source, its source hash, and the\n/// task-folder-targets map are threaded straight through the constructor — the same values the\n/// caller (mirroring <c>GraphCommand</c>'s <c>MermaidRenderer.RenderInteractive</c> /\n/// <c>TaskFolderTargets</c> calls) already computes from the live <c>PlanDefinition</c> — rather\n/// than re-parsing them back out of the already-written <c>diagram.html</c>'s embedded\n/// <c>&lt;script&gt;</c> tags. Threading is simpler and avoids a fragile round-trip through HTML/JSON\n/// that would break the moment the embedded markup's shape changes for an unrelated reason.\n/// </para>\n///\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Node-id scheme.</b> <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/>'s injective task-id → node-id-base\n/// allocation (collision-safe sanitize + <c>_2</c>/<c>_3</c>… disambiguation) is <c>private</c>, so\n/// this class reproduces it character-for-character (see <see cref=\"AllocateNodeIdBases\"/> /\n/// <see cref=\"Sanitize\"/>) to compute the SAME container id (<c>task_&lt;base&gt;</c>) and leaf ids\n/// (<c>task_&lt;base&gt;_pf_&lt;n&gt;</c> / <c>task_&lt;base&gt;_gr_&lt;n&gt;</c>, <c>n</c> = the\n/// check's ordinal position when its task's <see cref=\"TaskNode.Preflights\"/>/\n/// <see cref=\"TaskNode.Guardrails\"/> are sorted ordinal by <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Name\"/>,\n/// exactly as <c>MermaidRenderer.AppendCheckNodes</c> emits them) that <c>diagram.html</c> already\n/// embeds, so a status badge lands on the right SVG node.\n/// </para>\n///\n/// <para>\n/// This decorator's own status map is the only shared mutable state, and M4 worker threads may call\n/// in concurrently, so all access to it — and the write that projects from it — is serialised under\n/// one lock, mirroring <see cref=\"OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver\"/>. Renders are best-effort: a render\n/// failure (e.g. a transient file lock, or a bad output path) is swallowed so a UX nicety never\n/// flips a task's outcome or aborts the run.\n/// </para>\n///\n/// <para>\n/// <b>MINIMAL STUB (this task authors failing tests only).</b> <see cref=\"WriteDiagram\"/> always\n/// throws <see cref=\"NotImplementedException\"/> — the real re-render (calling\n/// <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/> and writing it to <c>diagram.html</c>) is\n/// <c>04-implement-diagram-observer</c>'s job. Every status-map/node-id bookkeeping method above is\n/// real (not stubbed) so the authored tests encode the CORRECT expected node ids/statuses and turn\n/// green the moment <see cref=\"WriteDiagram\"/> is implemented for real.\n/// </para>\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class OnTheFlyDiagramObserver : IRunObserver\n{\n    private readonly IRunObserver _inner;\n    private readonly string _diagramHtmlPath;\n    private readonly string _mermaidSource;\n    private readonly string _sourceHash;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> _taskFolderTargets;\n\n    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TaskNode> _tasksById;\n    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> _nodeIdBaseByTaskId;\n\n    // Per-node status word (container + leaf check ids).
